chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered the mosque while some of his companions were there, and he said: “Do you know what your Lord has said?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.”

He said: “Indeed, your Lord says: These five obligatory prayers—whoever performs them at their appointed times and preserves them, he shall meet Me on the Day of Resurrection, and with Me he shall have a covenant by which I will admit him into Paradise. And whoever does not perform them at their appointed times and does not preserve them, then that is up to Me: if I will, I punish him, and if I will, I forgive him.”
ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about performing the five obligatory prayers on time?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the great status of the five obligatory salat (prayers) and the importance of performing them in their proper times while guarding them consistently. It promises entry into Paradise for the one who maintains them, and warns that neglecting them leaves a person subject to Allah’s judgment on the Day of Resurrection.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.625 - "The Messenger of Allah (sw) entered the mosque where some of his companions were present and said:
"Do you know what your Lord (azj) has said?"
They replied: "Allah (swt) and His Messenger know best."

He (sw) said: "Your Lord (azj) says:
'These five obligatory prayers—whoever performs them at their appointed times and maintains them, will meet Me on the Day of Judgment with a promise from Me to admit him into Paradise. And whoever does not perform them at their appointed times and does not maintain them, then that is up to Me—if I wish, I will punish him, and if I wish, I will forgive him.'"
